title: Rolling Version Relay with Traffic Percentage Decoupling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an automated, Terraform-first upgrade path for private (VPC) control planes that performs rolling minor-version promotions using a lightweight relay proxy that decouples traffic percentage from instance promotion. This ticket delivers: 1) Terraform module and CI job to create/coordinate versioned controlplane deployments; 2) a Relay component (stateless proxy) that can slice traffic by percentage and route to specific control plane version endpoints; 3) health-gating and automated promotion/rollback rules driven by Prometheus metrics and synthetic user probes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Terraform modules can provision two parallel controlplane versions (vX and vX+1) in a customer's VPC with no manual steps. 2) Relay routes a configurable percentage of production traffic to vX+1 while keeping remainder on vX. 3) Health gates automatically promote from 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% given green signals, and roll back on predefined error thresholds. 4) End-to-end tests (integration + chaos + soak) pass in staging. 5) Console shows per-version token/latency/cost breakdown and rollout status. 6) Runbook and SLOs documented and sign-off from Security/Infra.
technical_design:
High level design:
- Terraform-driven orchestration: new module private/controlplane_upgrade that creates versioned stacks, IAM roles, and Relay target groups. Module exposes inputs for image tag, instance profile, and canary policy.
- Relay component: small Envoy-based proxy with percent-based routing rules stored in Consul KV (or SSM parameter for AWS) and updated via Terraform apply or a rollout controller. Relay is deployed as a lightweight HA pair inside customer subnet and supports TLS and mutual auth to controlplanes.
- Promotion controller: Kubernetes job (internal infra k8s) or Lambda that reads metrics + synthetic probe statuses and advances percentage per policy. It uses the Terraform state (or a dedicated metadata store in the control plane) to ensure idempotency.
- Health gating: Prometheus rules + Alertmanager webhooks feed the promotion controller. Metrics: 5xx rate, p50/p95 latency delta vs baseline, error-rate on auth failures, tail latency regressions, and synthetic probe success ratio.
- Rollback strategy: automatic rollback to previous version if any gate trips during a promotion or if cumulative error delta > 1.5x baseline for 10 minutes. Manual abort button in Console triggers immediate rollback.
- Observability: add labels for version to all traces/tokens to enable per-version comparisons in Grafana dashboards.
- Security: Relay and promotion controller require KMS envelope encryption for state, and Terraform module must validate that customer KMS key is provided or fails; security review required before GA.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): wire Terraform module + Relay in our staging VPC, run scripted promotions to verify percentage transitions. Phase 2 (pilot customers): enable on 2 trusted customers with low traffic profiles, run 24h soak on each stage. Phase 3 (wider beta): open for self-serve private customers with feature flag and support. Phase 4 (GA): after error budget analysis and security sign-offs. Promotion policy default: 0% -> 5% (2h soak) -> 25% (4h soak) -> 60% (6h soak) -> 100% (final). Each soak has guard rails and max-failure thresholds. Manual hold and rollback available at each stage.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for Terraform modules (terratest).
- Integration test: full deploy of v1 and v2 stacks in ephemeral VPC, Relay injected, scripted traffic generator to simulate production mix.
- Synthetic probes: exercise controlplane APIs (auth, token issue, model routing) from multiple AZs.
- Chaos tests: kill controlplane nodes during canary to validate failover and rollback triggers.
- Soak: 72h soak at 25% and 24h soak at 60% for pilot customers.
- Security: run static scans of Relay image and IaC checks; run threat model review with Security team.
risks_and_mitigations: 1) Relay becomes single point of failure: mitigate with HA pairs + cross-AZ LB + health checks. 2) Terraform state drift between versions: mitigation - use pre-flight validation job and a small reconciliation controller. 3) Telemetry noise causes false rollbacks: use smoothing windows and require multiple independent signals (synthetic + production metrics). 4) Customer network constraints (NAT/ACL): provide fallback where Relay can be deployed as sidecar or as customer-managed proxy. 5) KMS/key access issues block promotions: add a validation step in module to test KMS permissions on apply.
implementation_notes:
- Terraform path: modules/private/controlplane_upgrade/* (module to author).
- Relay: repo infra/relay-service (Dockerfile, envoy config, health endpoints).
- Promotion controller: repo infra/promotion-controller, will have a dry-run mode.
- Add tags/labels: redwood.controlplane.version and redwood.rollout.stage for telemetry.
- PR checklist: terratest coverage, runbook link, Grafana dashboard snapshot, and Security sign-off checkbox.
- Concurrency: ensure promotion controller uses optimistic locking on metadata key to avoid double-promote race.
runbook:
Runbook location: Confluence page (see links). Quick actions:
- Abort promotion: run /promote abort or press 'Abort' in Console -> triggers Terraform apply to re-route 100% to previous version.
- Emergency rollback: toggle feature flag 'force-rollback' and notify customer success.
- Investigate: check per-version traces and token breakdown, check synthetic probe history, and inspect Relay logs for 502/503 spikes.
